images.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Photorealistic illustration of an explicit biblical comparison or event, first-century Roman Judea and Galilee, landscape 3:2, natural materials and daylight, anatomically coherent people with exactly two arms and animals with correct limbs; fully covering modest opaque robes. No modern objects, readable writing, portrait of God the Father, blood, injury or watermark. Galatians 1:18 says Paul visited Peter in Jerusalem and stayed with him for fifteen days. Two adult men Paul and Peter speak thoughtfully in a simple first-century Jerusalem household courtyard. Only two main people, no council or crowd, no invented travel calendar or writing. Paul is a travelling visitor with a small bag beside him; Peter welcomes him with restrained warmth. Historically plausible unadorned robes, distinct two arms each, no claim to exact portraits.

images.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Photorealistic illustration of an explicit biblical comparison or event, first-century Roman Judea and Galilee, landscape 3:2, natural materials and daylight, anatomically coherent people with exactly two arms and animals with correct limbs; fully covering modest opaque robes. No modern objects, readable writing, portrait of God the Father, blood, injury or watermark. Galatians 2:11–14: Paul publicly challenges Peter in Antioch for withdrawing from eating with Gentile believers. An adult Paul speaks seriously but without physical aggression to an adult Peter who stands by a shared dining table, while a small diverse group of adult believers listens. Peter looks reflective and uncomfortable. First-century Roman provincial courtyard in Antioch, not a medieval church. Clear coherent hands, no weapon, shouting, force or readable text. The focus is the open disagreement about shared meals, not Peter welcoming Paul.

images.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Photorealistic illustration of an explicit biblical comparison or event, first-century Roman Judea and Galilee, landscape 3:2, natural materials and daylight, anatomically coherent people with exactly two arms and animals with correct limbs; fully covering modest opaque robes. No modern objects, readable writing, portrait of God the Father, blood, injury or watermark. Galatians 4:13–14: Paul recalls being welcomed despite bodily illness when he first preached the gospel to the Galatians. A tired adult Paul sits fully clothed on a bench in a modest first-century Galatian home while two adult believers warmly receive him, offering a cup of water and a seat cushion. Exactly three adults, quiet hospitality and respect. No specific diagnosis, bleeding, wound, invented blindness or modern medical equipment. Paul remains attentive; the image illustrates the stated illness and welcome without inventing its cause.

images.scene: De gemeenten in Judea horen het bericht
images.alt: De gemeenten in Judea horen het bericht — Galaten 1:24; tekstillustratie.
images.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Photorealistic illustration of an explicit biblical comparison or event, first-century Roman Judea and Galilee, landscape 3:2, natural materials and daylight, anatomically coherent people with exactly two arms and animals with correct limbs; fully covering modest opaque robes. No modern objects, readable writing, portrait of God the Father, blood, injury or watermark. Galatians 1:22–24 explicitly says the Christian communities in Judea did not know Paul by face; they only heard that their former persecutor now proclaimed the faith, and glorified God because of him. Show a modest household group of Judean adult believers listening to an ordinary messenger, then giving thanks to God. PAUL IS ABSENT. No central apostle being welcomed, no Paul portrait, no handshake receiving Paul. Four adult believers seated and one modest adult messenger standing, several look up thankfully. First-century home, realistic coherent hands, no readable text.
